relevance_note: Dried-bloodspot metabolomics study whose Tables 1 and 2 list individual SSADHD patients with sex, age and ALDH5A1 genotype, e.g. '| 1 | 10 | F | p.W204* | p.R425* | CH |'.
method_note: Rows were built by a short Python script (scratch only) that copies Table 1 and Table 2 rows verbatim from the paper and assigns cells by column; every value was checked by hand against the tables, and every span was checked by script to occur verbatim. Labels: Tables 1 and 2 index patients by bare numbers in a 'Patient' column, so labels are 'Table 1 #n' and 'Table 2 #n'. The Table 2 note states 'Patients 1 and 2 identical to patients 1 and 2 in Table 1', so Table 2 patients 1 and 2 are recorded once, as 'Table 1 #1' and 'Table 1 #2'; Table 2 patients 3-7 are separate people (the text says the only newborn/post-newborn overlap is a single sibship). 22 individuals in all (17 post-newborn + 5 newborn-only). Tables 3 and 4 (metabolite values per DBS) have no patient label column and cannot be linked to Table 1/2 patients (ages differ from Table 1; Table 3 rows are DBS samples, not people), so no individuals or features were taken from them. Ages: Table 1 'Age (year)' and Table 2 'Current age (year)' recorded as age at last evaluation; Table 1 patient 5 has a blank age. No individual clinical features (seizures, ID, etc.) are reported for any patient, so all 20 checklist items are 'not reported' for everyone; phenotypic_features hold only biochemical findings from the GHB columns, the white-cell SSADH activity notes (patients 3 and 4) and the footnote-b urine organic acids of Table 2 patient 5. Variants: Table 1 patients 5 and Table 2 patient 4 have 'NA' (not available) for both mutations: no variant rows. Table 1 patient 8 has 'See legend': the legend says exon 1 could not be amplified, 'suggesting a homozygous deletion (MLPA confirmation pending)', so one row with variant_original_string 'not reported' and zygosity not reported. Homozygous ('HZ') patients get one row. Table 1 patient 10 prints Mutation 1 as 'p.T233 M' (with a space) and Mutation 2 as 'p.T233M'; recorded once as 'p.T233M'. Footnote letters were dropped from values ('c.1054-2A>Ca' -> c.1054-2A>C; 'p.G441Rc' -> p.G441R); the footnote 'a' means differ between Table 1 (splice, considered pathogenic) and Table 2 (splice site SNP at the intron 6/exon 7 junction), and were applied only to the variant carrying the marker in that table (Table 2 patient 7's c.1054-2A>C has no marker, so no type/pathogenicity). Variant types are not stated except for those splice footnotes; none derived from HGVS. 'See above' functional notes (patients 10, 12, 14, 16, 17) were linked to the note above that names the same allele, with both spans. Inheritance is not reported for anyone. Contradictions in the paper: (1) the Table 1 note lists sibships 'patients 2 and 3; 9 and 10; 11 and 12; and 15-17', but patients 2 and 3 have different genotypes (CH p.W204*/p.R425* vs HZ p.W204*), while patients 1 and 2 share a genotype and the text describes the overlapping newborn sibship as patients 1 and 2 of Table 2; (2) the text says '4 sibships (total, 8 patients)', but the listed sibships total 9 patients; (3) the note says all sibships were 'confirmed by sequencing of the parents', but patients 11 and 12 are marked 'CH (parents untested)'; (4) the text gives post-newborn ages 0.8-38 years while Table 1 lists ages up to 40. Family labels were not recorded (the paper gives none). publications: n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated left null because the authors state 17 post-newborn and 7 newborn patients separately but never a single total; cites_prior_report left null because the paper does not state that these patients were described earlier ('representing ~10% of published cases' and the reference after patient 14's note are ambiguous).
